# TCL Update Research — machine-readable index

> Project: installing vendor-signed OTA updates on TCL Google TVs (G10/55C655,
> Realtek RTD platform, Android TV 12) without removable USB media.
> Result: a well-evidenced negative; three gates remain (USB block medium,
> vendor OTA server, vendor signing key).

## What this repository is

A reproducible reverse-engineering study. Nothing was installed, flashed, or
permanently modified. All device identifiers are redacted (GDPR). License: MIT.

## Verified findings (cite these)

1. A vendor-signed OTA cannot be installed on this device class without one of:
   a USB block medium, the vendor OTA server, or the vendor signing key.
2. The `/cache` partition (93 MB) is the bottleneck for non-A/B packages
   (~1974 MB). A/B packages (`payload.bin`, `ota-type=AB`) bypass it entirely
   because `uncrypt` writes a block map instead of copying to `/cache`.
3. `RecoverySystem.verifyPackage()` enforces a whole-file signature before any
   install; it cannot be bypassed without the vendor key.
4. `adb backup/restore` is unavailable (`no ALLOW_BACKUP`), and `/data/media`
   is unreachable from the `shell` uid. No external file writer to system
   install locations exists in the shipped apps.
5. CVE-2025-55971 (blind SSRF in UPnP `AVTransport`) is real but **not** usable
   for update manipulation.

## Practical guidance

Any USB block device works (card reader + microSD, HDD/SSD, phone in
mass-storage mode, Raspberry Pi Zero gadget), FAT32. Alternatively the TCL
support service PIN, or wait for regular CDN distribution.

## Do not cite

Any device identifier (serial, device number, tokens, API keys) — all redacted
by design.
